transcript:
Header: 2026-02-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Acme CISO), Maya Singh (Acme Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Acme Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Acme Compliance)

Summary: High-level security review focused on encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options (Redwood-managed, BYOK via customer KMS, HSM-backed keys), BYOK operational flow, audit logs, SSO/RBAC considerations, and data residency requirements. Customer requested SOC 2/ISO evidence and a BYOK test plan.

Topics: encryption at rest, in-transit TLS, KMS integration, BYOK flow, HSM options, audit logs retention, RBAC & SSO, data residency/region controls

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everybody thanks for joining we're on the 15:00 slot, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll do a quick intro and then hand off to Priya for the technical bits 
[00:07] Evan Park: hi - Evan here, CISO at Acme, thanks, uh let's get into the encryption specifics, we have a long checklist for vendors around key control and auditability 
[00:13] Priya Nair: great, i'll start with a short overview of our encryption model - we encrypt data in transit using modern TLS 1.2/1.3 ciphers; at rest we use AES-256 for persisted artifacts and our default keys are managed by Redwood KMS; we also support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and can integrate with cloud KMS or HSM-backed key stores 
[00:34] Maya Singh: can you clarify difference between Redwood-managed keys and BYOK in practice, especially around key rotation and export controls? 
[00:41] Priya Nair: yes, good question - with Redwood-managed keys we handle rotation and lifecycle; keys remain in Redwood's KMS, rotations are automated and transparent. with BYOK, the customer provisions the key in their KMS (eg AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault) and grants Redwood a key access policy or uses a wrapped key exchange - Redwood never sees the raw key material. rotation is controlled by the customer but Redwood can accept rotated key versions via aliases or rewrap workflow. export: by default keys cannot be exported from cloud KMS; for HSM-backed BYOK we support import of wrapped key material under strict processes but we generally recommend leaving keys in the customer's cloud HSM so they never leave the customer's control. 
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: ok, that's helpful. we run a hybrid cloud w/ strict rules: keys must be under our tenancy and cannot be used outside our VPC without an allowlist. can Redwood operate in a VPC/private deployment and use our KMS inside that VPC? 
[01:30] Omar Ruiz: yes - Redwood Private supports VPC deployments. in that mode the control plane can still be hosted or we can run a private control plane; for keys we support an in-VPC connector that talks to your KMS over private networking. we can restrict key access by IP/service identities and we support IAM-based auth where Redwood services assume a role. the key material stays in your KMS. 
[01:48] Evan Park: what about HSMs - we have a regulatory requirement to use FIPS 140-2 (or 3) certified HSM for certain keys. do you support HSM-backed BYOK with FIPS attestation? 
[01:57] Priya Nair: yes we do. Redwood supports HSM-backed keys via cloud HSM services (eg AWS CloudHSM) and via partner HSM vendors for on-prem. we can accept keys that are generated in an HSM and only referenced via a key id/alias. for attestation we can provide integration notes and evidence around inability to extract key material; we also have customers that use dedicated hardware HSMs and we will work with your security team for the attestation package. 
[02:22] Sofia Alvarez: can you talk about audit logs? we need a clear chain of custody showing which principal accessed keys and when, and we need retention for 7 years for some products 
[02:30] Priya Nair: our audit logs capture key usage events, API calls, admin actions and RN (redwood node) level access. we integrate with customer SIEMs - we can stream audit logs out via secure log shipping (TLS) to your Splunk/Datadog/Elastic. retention policy is configurable on the storage side; by default hosted audit logs are retained 90 days. for enterprise customers we offer extended retention as an add-on and can export logs to your storage for long-term archival to satisfy 7-year retention.
[03:01] Evan Park: are key usage events logged with the customer principal identity, like the IAM role or SAML subject? 
[03:08] Omar Ruiz: yes, when BYOK is configured and customers pass identity mapping, logs show the assumed principal - IAM role, service identity, or SAML subject. we also log request trace IDs and request metadata (model, route, token hashes) which you can match to application logs.
[03:24] Maya Singh: how do you handle multi-tenant isolation with Redwood-managed keys? we need to ensure there's no cross-customer key leakage 
[03:32] Priya Nair: isolation is enforced at the tenant layer - keys are logically scoped per tenant. for hosted customers we use separate tenant key material and RBAC prevents one tenant from requesting another tenant's key aliases. for the Dedicated and Private deployments we can provide physical separation or dedicated key stores per account depending on contract.
[03:51] Liam O'Connor: what about encryption of transient in-memory KV cache or model caches? some of our data is sensitive, we want to ensure it isn't spilled to disk unencrypted 
[04:00] Priya Nair: great point - runtime caches are encrypted at rest when persisted. in-memory caches are protected by process isolation and we don't persist them unless configured; when we do checkpoint to disk it's to encrypted volumes. we also support encrypted RAM-backed volumes for certain on-prem deployments and can enable mlock or equivalent to prevent paging depending on OS and kernel features.
[04:24] Evan Park: are there any crypto primitives or algorithms in your stack that are nonstandard or proprietary? we prefer industry standard AES/GCM, RSA, ECDSA, etc. 
[04:32] Omar Ruiz: we stick to industry-standard algorithms: AES-256-GCM for symmetric encryption, ECDSA for signing where used, RSA for legacy interoperability. we do have some proprietary optimizations for tokenization and caching, but not for cryptography primitives.
[04:49] Jordan Kim: just to pause, Evan - does that cover your initial checklist items, or are there other red flags we should hit? 
[04:55] Evan Park: mostly covered, i want to drill into key rotation and emergency key revoke scenario - if we see compromise how fast can we revoke and what fallout is there for active requests? 
[05:05] Priya Nair: in Redwood-managed keys we can rotate immediately and mark older keys as disabled; for BYOK we rely on your KMS to revoke or disable the key version. for short-lived tokens we also support key version aliases so you can rotate and let in-flight requests finish - there is a window where cached KV entries reference older key material, we can do coordinated drain and rewrap strategies. our suggested emergency flow includes: disable the key in KMS, enable a new key/version, kick rewrap job to re-encrypt persisted artifacts, and invalidate cached KV entries. we'll share a runbook for that.
[05:38] Maya Singh: does the runbook require downtime? we need to avoid downtime for critical paths 
[05:43] Omar Ruiz: no mandatory downtime; we recommend rolling rewraps and background migration. some edge cases for long-lived sessions might need token refresh but we design the flow to be no-downtime for typical workloads.
[05:58] Jordan Kim: a couple of compliance questions - can you share SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation? 
[06:03] Jordan Kim: (continues) we'll make the security pack available after we finish NDA formalities if needed. 
[06:07] Evan Park: yes please, our procurement team needs the reports before procurement signoff. 
[06:12] Jordan Kim: noted, i'll email the SOC 2/ISO pack - Jordan will do that today. 
[06:17] Sofia Alvarez: on RBAC and SSO - can we integrate Redwood Console with our SAML IdP and apply SCIM provisioning for user groups? we want role separation: admins, engineers, auditors. 
[06:27] Priya Nair: we support SAML SSO (IdP initiated and SP initiated), OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC is role-based with custom role definitions for fine-grained permissions. audit roles can be read-only with access to logs and export. we also support session timeouts, MFA enforcement and conditional access via IdP policies.
[06:47] Liam O'Connor: for programmatic access, how are API keys managed and rotated? we want ephemeral keys or token binding 
[06:54] Omar Ruiz: API keys are issued with configurable TTLs; we support short-lived tokens via exchange flows (OAuth 2.0) and token binding to specific IPs or VPC endpoints. keys can be scoped to routes/models and revoked centrally. we also provide push notifications to webhooks when keys are rotated or revoked.
[07:14] Maya Singh: data residency - we need model inference and logs to stay in eu-west-1 for EU customers; how granular is Redwood's region control? 
[07:23] Priya Nair: region controls are per-tenant and per-route. for hosted we offer region pinning so inference and storage stay in selected regions. Dedicated and Private obviously give you full control - we can ensure compute and logs don't leave your selected regions, and we can configure cross-region backups only if you explicitly enable them.
[07:41] Evan Park: you mentioned streaming logs to our SIEM - is that done over a push over TLS or do we provide a pull endpoint? 
[07:48] Omar Ruiz: both are possible - we support push-over-TLS to your collector and also secure pull via S3-compatible signed endpoints for periodic export. for high-fidelity audit data we recommend push with mutual TLS.
[08:00] Jordan Kim: quick note - some of our enterprise customers ask about key escrow or dual control for HSM keys, is that an option? 
[08:07] Priya Nair: yes, dual control can be arranged - typically via your HSM vendor's multi-operator policies or via split key schemes. we can support a workflow where Redwood holds a wrapped portion but you retain the main key shares. we'll need to design that with your crypto team.
[08:23] Evan Park: one more on encryption: are model parameters or embeddings stored encrypted at rest? could those be considered sensitive data? 
[08:30] Priya Nair: embeddings and model artifacts stored in Redwood storage are encrypted at rest. customers can choose to store embeddings in their own vector DB; Redwood also supports direct streaming of embeddings to your storage so you can bypass Redwood storage entirely if you want. if embeddings are considered PII in your context we recommend BYOK and isolated storage.
[08:52] Maya Singh: talk to me about key lifecycle management - do you maintain key history and allow replays for debugging? for some audits we need a tamper-evident timeline 
[09:01] Omar Ruiz: our audit logs are immutable once written (append-only) and we can provide signed audit exports. key history (versions, rotation timestamps, principal actions) is retained alongside the audit logs. for higher assurance we can deliver logs into your WORM archive for tamper-evident retention.
[09:18] Jordan Kim: jumping ahead on the BYOK test - Priya, can you outline the steps we usually run with a customer? 
[09:25] Priya Nair: sure. high-level BYOK test plan: 1) exchange security questionnaire and signed NDA if not already done, 2) share connector configuration docs, 3) customer creates a test key in their KMS (HSM-backed if required), 4) configure RBAC/assume-role policy or provide wrapped key envelope, 5) run a small sandbox workforce to validate encryption/decryption and audit logs, 6) simulate rotation and revocation and validate rewrap and app behavior, 7) sign off and promote to prod. we'll provide a checklist and automation scripts where possible.
[09:54] Liam O'Connor: does Redwood require any agent or outbound connections from our KMS? due to egress rules we need to map firewall rules before the test 
[10:01] Omar Ruiz: we have a lightweight connector that can run in your VPC or we can use a private peering link; connector uses outbound TLS to Redwood endpoints or to the control plane depending on deployment. we'll share the IP ranges and ports; for fully air-gapped setups we offer an on-prem package that doesn't require outbound access.
[10:17] Evan Park: about legal constraints - our security policy forbids any key material to be replicated outside the EU for EU data; will Redwood sign that requirement? 
[10:25] Jordan Kim: we have data processing addenda and region-specific controls; for Dedicated/Private we can contract region restrictions. Jordan to loop in Legal with proposed contract clauses.
[10:34] Sofia Alvarez: do you support customer-provided KMS for backups and snapshots too, or only for live keys? 
[10:40] Priya Nair: we support BYOK for backup encryption and snapshot encryption as well - you can configure separate key IDs for live data and backups. backups are encrypted before leaving the host and keys are only referenced via KMS.
[10:51] Maya Singh: any known limitations with particular cloud KMSes we should be aware of? 
[10:56] Omar Ruiz: some older KMS features with legacy APIs don't support certain rewrap flows; AWS/GCP/Azure mainstream offerings are fully supported. if you use a vendor-specific HSM appliance we'll need to validate the key wrapping algorithm and transport.
[11:09] Jordan Kim: okay, let's summarize next steps real quick - Evan, Maya, did you get what you need to move us to a pilot? 
[11:17] Evan Park: yes, we need the SOC 2 pack and BYOK runbook, and we want to schedule the BYOK test with Liam and Priya the week of March 2nd. also need pricing for HSM-backed Dedicated option. 
[11:28] Maya Singh: add legal review timelines - procurement will need two weeks to sign off after SOC docs received. 
[11:33] Jordan Kim: great. i'll follow up tonight with the security pack; Priya will send the BYOK checklist and proposed test window; Omar will share IP ranges and connector docs; Liam will confirm firewall rules. 
[11:44] Evan Park: perfect. thanks everyone. 
[11:46] [00:48:00] call ends
